transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-27
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Emma (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM), Maya (NovaEdge Head of ML), Liam (Platform Eng), Priya (FinOps), Tom (Security)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage, cost attribution, and how Redwood can map costs back to product routes. Customer is evaluating hosted + pilot of Dedicated for latency-sensitive routes. They asked about audit logs, KMS integration, and sample billing exports.

[00:00] Emma (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'll kick us off, quick agenda: overview of the console, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and then ravi will do a short deep dive into routing behavior and dedicated options. sound good?
[00:08] Maya (NovaEdge): yep, sounds good — we have like 45 minutes, want to focus on the cost mapping stuff, and then security questions at the end.
[00:13] Liam: also want to see how retention and sampling affects cost and observability — we take a lot of small inference calls.
[00:18] Emma: awesome. quick context for you all — novaedge is evaluating us for a pilot, right? priya, can you confirm timeline?
[00:22] Priya: yeah we're trying to have a pilot in the next 3–4 weeks, budget sign-off depends on seeing per-route economics.
[00:27] Emma: perfect. ravi, i'll hand over to you for the console tour.

[00:30] Ravi (Redwood SE): great, sharing screen now — okay heading into the console, top-left is the routes view. you can see routes are first-class objects — each route has its own model pin, batching policy, and egress region. here's a customer example, notice the traffic split and the 95th p50 latency histogram.
[00:55] Maya: small note, is that histogram from real-time traces or aggregated daily metrics?
[00:59] Ravi: it's aggregated at 1-min granularity for the last 24 hours by default, we also keep raw traces for 7 days in hosted, longer for dedicated if you opt in.
[01:07] Liam: raw traces meaning full tokens + prompt? any pii concerns?
[01:12] Ravi: good call — by default we mask/obfuscate user prompts in hosted, and we provide a data retention toggle on the route; for private deployments you can keep raw KV for internal debugging but it's encrypted with your KMS.
[01:23] Tom: so KMS integration works with AWS KMS and GCP KMS? any HSM?
[01:28] Ravi: yes AWS/GCP KMS supported, HSM via enterprise integrations — i'll send the security doc, we have a short appendix on supported key stores.

[01:35] Emma: on the per-route billing page — this is the feature priya wanted. you can map tokens to cost units by model variant and hardware, and then allocate those costs to a product route.
[01:46] Priya: is allocation done in near-real-time? we need daily breakdowns but ideally hourly.
[01:51] Ravi: allocations are computed post-fact — we stream usage to a cost-engine, which emits hourly rollups for routes. those are then visible in the per-route ledger and exportable as CSV or parquet.
[02:01] Priya: do you support cost tags we already use in our infra?
[02:04] Ravi: yes you can attach tags at request time or map internal metadata fields, and then the console's cost grouping respects those tags.

[02:10] [02:10] Maya: quick question on sampling, say we sample 10% of requests for QA traces — how does that affect billing attribution and dashboards?
[02:18] Ravi: good question — sampling only affects trace collection, not billing. billing is per-token, we bill all requests. sampling will reduce observability granularity but the console will show estimated extrapolated metrics next to sampled data so you can see error bars.
[02:33] Emma: we also surface a sampling confidence score — helpful for small-volume routes.
[02:38] Liam: what about prefix caching? our chat prompt often repeats large system messages, can that reduce cost?
[02:44] Ravi: yes, prefix/KV caching is a big lever. in the console you'll see a "cache hit" metric and an estimated token-savings projection. if you enable caching at the route level we'll show the historical savings and recommend cache ttl.
[02:58] Maya: neat. how do you recommend we split hosted vs dedicated? we have a few ultra-low-latency routes and lots of background embedding jobs.
[03:05] Ravi: common pattern: host user-facing, latency-sensitive routes on Dedicated (reserved GPUs) and keep batch/embeddings on hosted to benefit from elasticity. the console can show a cost-sim comparison: keep-run both options for 30 days and it will estimate unit cost including reserved capacity amortization.
[03:24] Emma: i'll note that for your pilot we can configure two routes — one pinned to a dedicated pool and one to hosted — and show side-by-side economics.

[03:30] [03:30] Priya: do you have sample spreadsheets for finance review?
[03:33] Emma: yes — we have a pricing sheet template and a unit economics workbook, i'll attach it after.
[03:38] Maya: security question — what does audit logging look like? can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[03:42] Ravi: audit logs include per-request metadata (route, model, userID hash, status). exports to Kafka/S3 are supported; for Private you can syslog to your SIEM.
[03:52] Tom: any SOC2/ISO artifacts we can review?
[03:55] Emma: yes sent previously but i'll re-share the security pack, it includes SOC2 cert, pen test summary, and data flow diagrams.

[04:01] Ravi: switching to the route-level cost breakdown now — on the left you can filter by model, region, and time window. the main graph shows token consumption by role: prompt vs completion tokens, embeddings, and KV cache hits. below that is a cost-ladder that maps model variant -> hardware type -> per-token cost.
[04:20] Maya: curious about quantization — do cost estimates reflect using quantized variants?
[04:24] Ravi: yes if you pin a quantized model variant we'll show estimated throughput and cost delta; note that quantization sometimes affects quality so we link to evaluation regression alerts in Optimize.
[04:36] Liam: for billing exports can we get a breakdown that ties token usage to our internal product IDs?
[04:40] Ravi: absolutely — you can inject a product_id header in requests and our exports will include that. the console also supports a mapping layer if you want to translate route names to product teams.

[04:48] [04:48] Maya: what does the UX look like for anomaly detection — we had weird spikes last quarter and need alerting tied to cost thresholds.
[04:55] Ravi: alerts can be route-level or account-level. you can set per-route spend thresholds, and we have anomaly detection that groups spikes by model/version and top-k callers. alerts can route to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook.
[05:07] Priya: can we create daily cap enforcement? if a route hits x dollars stop it or fall back to cheaper model?
[05:12] Ravi: yes — policy engine supports hard cap (reject) and soft-fallback (route to lower-cost model). we also have canary rollout control to gradually move traffic during model swaps.

[05:20] Emma: i'll demo the exports now — clicking export, choose hourly parquet, include product_id and tags. you can also download a sample billing CSV that maps to our recommended chargeback format.
[05:34] Liam: nice. who typically owns the cost-engine — is that on your side?
[05:38] Ravi: Redwood runs the hosted cost-engine. for Private, we ship the same components but they run in your VPC so you control storage retention.
[05:46] Maya: any limitations on number of routes? we have thousands of micro-routes across product lines.
[05:50] Ravi: no hard limit, we advise grouping micro-routes under logical prefixes and using sampling for very low-volume ones to keep UI noise down. the backend scales, but UX is better with some grouping.

[05:58] [05:58] Tom: compliance — can we restrict who sees route payloads? need RBAC per team.
[06:03] Ravi: yes RBAC is role-based at route and model level, you can scope teams to only see their product routes and anonymize request contents.
[06:09] Maya: do you support SAML/SSO?
[06:11] Emma: yep SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning.

[06:15] [06:15] (Ravi demos a quick scenario: create two routes, one pinned to dedicated pool)
[06:21] Ravi: here we create route /chat/fast pinned to pool-1, and /embed/batch to hosted. you can see the per-route projected cost per 1M tokens.
[06:30] Priya: that projected cost — what's assumed for GPU amortization?
[06:33] Ravi: we provide two modes: amortize reserved capacity across pinned routes or show full pool-level amortization. for pilot we usually run both so finance can decide allocation method.
[06:45] Maya: can we simulate 30 days of traffic to get comparative run-costs?
[06:49] Ravi: yes in the console run the "cost-sim" with your traffic profile CSV, it'll output expected spend and per-token latency distribution.

[06:56] Emma: quick note on data residency — if you need EU-only, we can pin routes to eu-central and enforce region routing.
[07:03] Liam: that helps. any egress cost surprises for embeddings that we should know?
[07:07] Ravi: embeddings are large, so network egress might add up if you're moving payloads cross-region; the cost-sim includes an egress column if you simulate cross-region.
[07:16] Maya: thanks. this is covering most of our questions — tom, any more sec questions?
[07:20] Tom: just one — do you support customer-managed encryption keys for logs?
[07:24] Ravi: yes CMK for logs in Private, hosted we support envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for stored artifacts.

[07:31] Emma: moving to wrap-up — recap: we'll give you sandbox access with two pre-configured routes (dedicated + hosted), attach the pricing workbook, and ravi will build a sample per-route dashboard using a subset of your traffic.
[07:44] Maya: great. timeline again? pilot in 3–4 weeks?
[07:48] Priya: yes, finance needs the workbook by early next week for initial review.
[07:52] Emma: i'll get that out tomorrow. ravi will kick off sandbox setup.
[07:56] Liam: one more ask — can you surface top 10 expensive callers in the UI? that would help product owners.
[08:01] Ravi: yes that's already in the route insights tab, top callers by spend, and you can drill into request traces.

[08:07] (small cross-talk, people exchanging goodbyes)
[08:12] Emma: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
[08:15] Maya: thanks, bye.

Notes/attachments referenced: "Pilot pricing workbook (link)", "Security pack (link)", "Sample billing exports (link)"
